description: An industrial frontier. Sage flats and badlands with a rail line through them; the store keeps the credit, the post keeps the peace, and something was here before either.

appearance.storekeeper: Between you and the shelves, with the credit book already open.
appearance.prospector: Burnt the same colour all over, and carrying more than he can lift twice.
appearance.assayer: Weighing something very small and refusing to say what it came to.
appearance.marshal: Standing where he can see the door and the window at once.
appearance.deputy: Young, armed, and standing a half-step behind somebody older.
appearance.barkeep: Wiping the same six inches of counter through the entire conversation.
appearance.cardsharp: Dealing to nobody, one-handed, while he decides about you.
appearance.teamster: Smells of mules and axle grease, and is not apologising for either.
appearance.freight agent: A manifest, a pencil, and a train that is late again.
appearance.liveryman: Talking to a horse in the voice most people save for children.
appearance.cattleman: Sun-cut at the eyes, and looking past you at the weather.
appearance.seamstress: At the machine, and it does not stop for you.
appearance.trooper: Off duty, boots off, belt hung on the bedpost.

talksAbout.storekeeper: what is owed, by whom, and since when
talksAbout.prospector: the claim, the assay, and the man who jumped it
talksAbout.assayer: the samples, and the ones he has been told not to discuss
talksAbout.marshal: who has come in on the rail this week, and who has not left
talksAbout.freight agent: the schedule, the washout at the bend, and whose freight is sitting in it
talksAbout.cardsharp: the game, the house, and what a stranger is good for
talksAbout.cattleman: the water, the fence, and the survey nobody agrees with

lore.title: The Line to Nowhere
lore.premise: The company laid forty miles of rail towards a strike that has since been quietly written off, and stopped paying the crews in the middle of the flats. The towns along it were built for a traffic that is not coming.
lore.era: the second year after the strike played out
lore.tone: dry, transactional, and one bad week from violence

ambient: The rail runs straight through all of this without appearing to notice it.
Dust comes up off the flats and hangs at about the height of a rider.
Something metal is ticking as it cools, and there is nothing here that should be warm.
Sage, after the rain, which is the one thing this country does well.
A survey stake, painted, in the middle of a great deal of nothing.

shop: Green beans. You roast them yourself or you go without.
Dented, in syrup, and the most valuable thing on the shelf.
Fifty, and the box has been opened once.
warehouse: Stencilled, and stacked away from the lamp.
Heavy, and there are a great many of them.
Undyed, and stiff enough to stand up on its own.
hall: Two ounces to the ton, which is not enough and everyone knows it.
smithy: Offcuts and failures, kept for remelting.
inn: Cut, coloured, and sold as neither.
Worn soft, and short by one.
barracks: Fifty, and the box has been opened once.
ruin: Somebody drove this, once, and was paid for it.
Company scrip. Nobody within a hundred miles will take it.

shop: Green beans. Everything else here is a luxury; this is not.
In syrup. Worth twice what the sign says and they know it.
Fifty. Sold to anybody, noted against everybody.
Forty feet of it, waxed against the wet.
Dented, but the shutter still works.
A page in the book with your name at the top of it.
smithy: Long enough for the job and the argument after it.
Second-hand. Somebody's initials are on the stock.
warehouse: Sold by weight, carried by the careful.
The company paid for these once already.
For a tent, a wagon cover, or a pair of trousers.
inn: Cut, coloured, and sold as neither.
Straw mattress, shared room, no questions.
stable: Enough for a week on the road.
Faded to no colour at all.
apothecary: Smells terrible. Closes a cut in a day.
Two drops. The label does not say how many are too many.
Cloudy, and warm to the touch.

bush: It will make anything smell of the flats, including you.
saguaro: Split it and it is better than it looks.
Cloudy, and it will keep you upright for an afternoon.
rock: Streaked, heavy, and worth an assay if you ever get to one.
It takes a hard edge and a harder spark.
rubble: Pulled out of something that was worth pulling apart.
deadTree: Split from a trunk that has been dead long enough to be dry.
gravel: Panned out of the wash, and mostly disappointment.
crops: Cut green and tied with its own straw.
Small, tough, and grown where corn should not be.
